You are jolly_ember22, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

[![Continuous integration](https://github.com/tamasfe/taplo/workflows/Continuous%20integration/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tamasfe/taplo/actions?query=workflow%3A%22Continuous+integration%22) [![Latest Version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/taplo.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/taplo) [![Documentation](https://docs.rs/taplo/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/taplo) [**Website**](https://taplo.tamasfe.dev) # Taplo This is the repository for Taplo, a TOML v1.0.0 toolkit, more details on the [website](https://taplo.tamasfe.dev). - [Taplo](#taplo) - [Status](#status) - [Contributing](#contributing) ## Status The project is very young, so bugs and incomplete features are expected, so [any help is welcome](CONTRIBUTING.md)! The correctness of the TOML parsing and decoding is not yet entirely guaranteed (as there is no official 1.0.0 compliance test suite yet). ## Contributing All kinds of contributions are welcome. Make sure to read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first! # Introduction Taplo CLI aims to be an one stop shop tool for working with TOML files via the command line. The features include validation, formatting, and querying TOML documents with a [jq](https://stedolan.github.io/jq/)-like fashion. # Formatting It is possible to format files in-place or via standard i/o. ```sh taplo fmt foo.toml ``` Or ```sh cat foo.toml | taplo fmt - ``` ::: info By default Taplo will bail on documents that contain syntax errors to avoid destructive edits, you can use the `--force` flag to suppress this and try to format the invalid document(s) anyway. ::: ## Options Formatter options are read from the [configuration file](./configuration.md#configuration-file), on top of that it is possible to specify overrides via the `--option` flag: ```sh taplo fmt --option indent_tables=false foo.toml ``` ## Check It is possible to check whether the given files are properly formatted via the `--check` flag. When this flag is supplied, no formatting will be done. # Conversion and Extraction Taplo makes it easy to convert TOML files to JSON and also extract specific values via the `get` command. ## Examples The following examples use the TOML file below: ```toml # foo.toml [foo] bar = true [[baz]] baz_field = "baz 1" [[baz]] baz_field = "baz 2" ``` ## Converting to JSON ```sh taplo get -f foo.toml -o json ``` This will yield the following output: ```json { "foo": { "bar": true }, "baz": [ { "baz_field": "baz 1" }, { "baz_field": "baz 2" } ] } ``` ## Extracting Specific Values It is possible to extract specific values via a simple query expressions. ```sh taplo get -f foo.toml 'baz[1].baz_field' ``` This will yield: ``` baz 2 ``` ::: warning Expressions with array patterns `[]` might need to be put between quotation marks for some shells. ::: ::: info List indexing is 0-based. ::: By default the value will be "parsed", so that no strings will contain escape sequences or quotation marks. However it is also possible to change the output format to JSON: ```sh taplo get -f foo.toml -o json baz ``` will yield: ```json [ { "baz_field": "baz 1" }, { "baz_field": "baz 2" } ] ``` ### More Examples More examples for query expressions using the same document above: | expression | output format | output | | :---------------: | :-----------: | :--------------------: | | `baz.0.baz_field` | json | `"baz 1"` | | `baz.*.baz_field` | json | `[ "baz 1", "baz 2" ]` | | `baz.1.baz_field` | value | `baz 2` | | `baz.1` | toml | `baz_field = "baz 2"` | ::: info The outputs have been slightly modified to fit into the table format. :::"}}}

# Validation

Taplo supports validation of TOML files, by default it will only look for syntax errors and some semantic errors such as duplicate keys.

```sh
taplo check foo.toml
```

## Schema Validation

Taplo supports validation via [JSON Schemas](https://json-schema.org) (Draft 4).

### Using a Specific Schema

```sh
taplo check --schema https://example.com/foo-schema.json foo.toml
```

### Using a Schema Catalog

Taplo supports schema catalogs such as the [JSON Schema Store](https://www.schemastore.org/json/) for retrieving schemas and matching them to files via file names.

You can enable this by either specifying a catalog via the `--schema-catalog` flag, or enabling the use of the default catalogs via `--default-schema-catalogs`.
# Configuration

## Log Level

Taplo uses the Rust `tracing` library for configurable logging features and respects the `RUST_LOG` environment variable. All logs regardless of log level are printed to the standard error output.

In most cases you might wish to disable logging below a certain log level.
As an example if you wish to only see error messages, you can do the following:

```sh
RUST_LOG=error taplo lint foo.toml
```

The available log levels:

- `trace`
- `debug`
- `info`
- `warn`
- `error`

## Configuration File

<!-- TODO: config link -->

Taplo CLI, by default, searches the current working directory for a Taplo configuration file. This behaviour can be disabled by either supplying `--no-auto-config` or `--config <path>` flags. The `TAPLO_CONFIG` environmental variable can also be used to set the configuration, but the `--config` flag will take precedence.

"""Shell completion output for the Taplo CLI."""
from completions_data import completion


def run(shell: str) -> int:

    if data is None:
        return 1
    import sys
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
    return 0

"""Implementation of Taplo's config subcommands."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys


def run(args):
    """Run a config command. Return True when the command was recognized."""
    if not args or args[0] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
        return False
    sub = args[0]
    if sub == "default":
        # The reference's generated default configuration is empty.
        return True
    if sub == "schema":
        path = Path(__file__).with_name("config_schema.json")
        sys.stdout.write(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return True
    return False

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/tomlmini.py
+"""Small TOML reader for runtimes without the Python 3.11 tomllib module."""
+import datetime
+import json
+import re
+
+
+class TomlError(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+def _bare_value(s):
+    s = s.strip()
+    if s == "true": return True
+    if s == "false": return False
+    if s.startswith(('"', "'")):
+        if s[0] == '"':
+            try: return json.loads(s)
+            except Exception as e: raise TomlError(str(e))
+        if len(s) < 2 or s[-1] != "'": raise TomlError("unterminated string")
+        return s[1:-1]
+    if s.startswith("[") and s.endswith("]"):
+        body=s[1:-1].strip()
+        return [] if not body else [_bare_value(x) for x in _split(body, ',') if x.strip()]
+    if s.startswith("{") and s.endswith("}"):
+        out={}
+        for item in _split(s[1:-1], ','):
+            if not item.strip(): continue
+            kv=_split(item, '=')
+            if len(kv)!=2: raise TomlError("invalid inline table")
+            out[_key(kv[0].strip())]=_bare_value(kv[1])
+        return out
+    raw=s.replace("_", "")
+    try:
+        if re.fullmatch(r"[+-]?0x[0-9a-fA-F]+", raw): return int(raw, 0)
+        if re.fullmatch(r"[+-]?0o[0-7]+", raw): return int(raw, 0)
+        if re.fullmatch(r"[+-]?0b[01]+", raw): return int(raw, 0)
+        if re.fullmatch(r"[+-]?\d+", raw): return int(raw)
+        if re.fullmatch(r"[+-]?(?:\d+\.\d*|\d*\.\d+|\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?", raw): return float(raw)
+    except ValueError: pass
+    token=s.replace("z", "+00:00").replace("Z", "+00:00")
+    try:
+        if "T" in token or "t" in token or " " in token: return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(token)
+        if ":" in token: return datetime.time.fromisoformat(token)
+        if re.match(r"\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d$", token): return datetime.date.fromisoformat(token)
+    except ValueError: pass
+    raise TomlError("invalid value")
+
+
+def _split(s, delim):
+    result=[]; start=0; stack=[]; q=None; esc=False
+    for i,c in enumerate(s):
+        if q:
+            if esc: esc=False
+            elif c=='\\' and q=='"': esc=True
+            elif c==q: q=None
+        elif c in ('"', "'"): q=c
+        elif c in '[{(': stack.append(c)
+        elif c in ']})':
+            if stack: stack.pop()
+        elif c==delim and not stack:
+            result.append(s[start:i]); start=i+1
+    result.append(s[start:]); return result
+
+
+def _key(s):
+    s=s.strip()
+    if s.startswith('"'): return json.loads(s)
+    if s.startswith("'"): return s[1:-1]
+    if not s or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", s): raise TomlError("invalid key")
+    return s
+
+
+def loads(text):
+    root={}; current=root; arrays={}; pending=""; depth=0; q=None; esc=False
+    for raw in text.splitlines():
+        line=raw.strip()
+        if not pending:
+            line=_split(line, '#')[0].strip()
+            if not line: continue
+        pending += (" " if pending else "") + line
+        # Detect an unfinished array / quoted string / inline table.
+        depth=0; q=None; esc=False
+        for c in pending:
+            if q:
+                if esc: esc=False
+                elif c=='\\' and q=='"': esc=True
+                elif c==q: q=None
+            elif c in ('"', "'"): q=c
+            elif c in '[{': depth+=1
+            elif c in ']}': depth-=1
+        if depth>0 or q: continue
+        line=pending; pending=""
+        if line.startswith('[[') and line.endswith(']]'):
+            path=[_key(k) for k in _split(line[2:-2], '.')]
+            node=root
+            for k in path[:-1]: node=node.setdefault(k,{})
+            node.setdefault(path[-1],[]).append({}); current=node[path[-1]][-1]; continue
+        if line.startswith('[') and line.endswith(']'):
+            path=[_key(k) for k in _split(line[1:-1], '.')]
+            node=root
+            for k in path: node=node.setdefault(k,{})
+            current=node; continue
+        kv=_split(line, '=')
+        if len(kv)<2: raise TomlError("expected key/value")
+        path=[_key(k) for k in _split(kv[0], '.')]
+        node=current
+        for k in path[:-1]: node=node.setdefault(k,{})
+        key=path[-1]
+        if key in node: raise TomlError("duplicate key")
+        node[key]=_bare_value('='.join(kv[1:]))
+    if pending: raise TomlError("incomplete value")
+    return root
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

"""Implementation of Taplo's config subcommands."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys

_COMMON = "Options:\n      --colors <COLORS>\n          [default: auto]\n\n          Possible values:\n          - auto:   Determine whether to colorize output automatically\n          - always: Always colorize output\n          - never:  Never colorize output\n\n      --verbose\n          Enable a verbose logging format\n\n      --log-spans\n          Enable logging spans\n\n  -h, --help\n          Print help (see a summary with '-h')\n"


def run(args):
    args = list(args)
    if not args or args[0] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
        sys.stdout.write("Operations with the Taplo config file\n\nUsage: taplo config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>\n\nCommands:\n  default  Print the default `.taplo.toml` configuration file\n  schema   Print the JSON schema of the `.taplo.toml` configuration file\n  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)\n\n" + _COMMON)
        return 0
    sub = args[0]
    if sub not in ("default", "schema"):
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{sub}'\n\nUsage: taplo config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        return 2
    if len(args) > 1 and args[1] not in ("-h", "--help"):
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{args[1]}' found\n\nUsage: taplo config {sub} [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        return 2
    if len(args) > 1:
        description = "Print the default `.taplo.toml` configuration file" if sub == "default" else "Print the JSON schema of the `.taplo.toml` configuration file"
        sys.stdout.write(f"{description}\n\nUsage: taplo config {sub} [OPTIONS]\n\n{_COMMON}")
        return 0
    if sub == "default":
        return 0
    sys.stdout.write(Path(__file__).with_name("config_schema.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return 0
PY

def main(argv):
    # Clap exposes these as global options, so accept them before or after a
    # subcommand. Their setting has no effect on plain-text command output.
    cleaned = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--colors":
            i += 2
            continue
        if arg.startswith("--colors=") or arg in ("--verbose", "--log-spans"):
            i += 1
            continue
        cleaned.append(arg)
        i += 1
    argv = cleaned
    if not argv:
        sys.stderr.write("Usage: taplo [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  lint         Lint TOML documents [aliases: check, validate]
  format       Format TOML documents [aliases: fmt]
  lsp          Language server operations
  config       Operations with the Taplo config file [aliases: cfg]
  get          Extract a value from the given TOML document
  toml-test    Start a decoder for `toml-test` (https://github.com/BurntSushi/toml-test)
  completions  Generate completions for Taplo CLI
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --colors <COLORS>  [default: auto] [possible values: auto, always, never]
      --verbose          Enable a verbose logging format
      --log-spans        Enable logging spans
  -h, --help             Print help (see more with '--help')
  -V, --version          Print version
")
        return 2
    if argv[0] in ("-h", "--help"):

Commands:

  toml-test    Start a decoder for `toml-test` (https://github.com/BurntSushi/toml-test)
  completions  Generate completions for Taplo CLI
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --colors <COLORS>
          [default: auto]

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Determine whether to colorize output automatically
          - always: Always colorize output
          - never:  Never colorize output

      --verbose
          Enable a verbose logging format

      --log-spans
          Enable logging spans

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
")
        return 2 if not argv else 0
    if "-V" in argv or "--version" in argv:
        print("taplo 0.10.0"); return 0
    if argv[0] == "help":
        target=argv[1] if len(argv)>1 else ""
        if target in ("format","fmt"): return _format(["--help"])
        if target in ("get","lint","check","validate"):

"""Implementation of Taplo's config subcommands."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys

_COMMON = "Options:
      --colors <COLORS>
          [default: auto]

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Determine whether to colorize output automatically
          - always: Always colorize output
          - never:  Never colorize output

      --verbose
          Enable a verbose logging format

      --log-spans
          Enable logging spans

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
"


def run(args):
    args = list(args)
    if not args:
        sys.stderr.write("Operations with the Taplo config file

Usage: taplo config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  default  Print the default `.taplo.toml` configuration file
  schema   Print the JSON schema of the `.taplo.toml` configuration file
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --colors <COLORS>  [default: auto]
      --verbose          Enable a verbose logging format
      --log-spans        Enable logging spans
  -h, --help             Print help (see more with '--help')
")
        return 2
    if args[0] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
        sys.stdout.write("Operations with the Taplo config file

Usage: taplo config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  default  Print the default `.taplo.toml` configuration file
  schema   Print the JSON schema of the `.taplo.toml` configuration file
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

" + _COMMON)
        return 0
    sub = args[0]
    if sub not in ("default", "schema"):
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{sub}'

Usage: taplo config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

For more information, try '--help'.
")
        return 2
    if len(args) > 1 and args[1] not in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{args[1]}' found

Usage: taplo config {sub} [OPTIONS]

For more information, try '--help'.
")
        return 2
    if len(args) > 1:
        description = "Print the default `.taplo.toml` configuration file" if sub == "default" else "Print the JSON schema of the `.taplo.toml` configuration file"
        sys.stdout.write(f"{description}

Usage: taplo config {sub} [OPTIONS]

{_COMMON}")
        return 0
    if sub == "default":
        return 0
    sys.stdout.write(Path(__file__).with_name("config_schema.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return 0

{"chunk_id":"1ea5fb","wall_time_seconds":0.00000369,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":4623,"output":""""Basic TOML lint command implementation."""
import datetime
import json
import re
import sys
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlparse

from tomltest import _find_eq, _key_parts, _parse, _strip_comment, _unclosed, _value, _split
from file_collect import collect_files


def _duplicates(source):
    scopes = {(): {}}
    table = ()
    array_indices = {}
    declared_tables = {}

    def resolve_table(parts):
        # A table nested below an array-of-tables belongs to the current array
        # element, so the same header may appear in each element.
        for size in range(len(parts) - 1, 0, -1):
            prefix = parts[:size]
            if prefix in array_indices:
                anchor = ("__array_table__", prefix, array_indices[prefix])
                return (anchor,) + parts[size:]
        return parts

    for number, raw in enumerate(source.splitlines(), 1):
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if line.startswith("[[") and line.endswith("]]" ):
            name = tuple(_key_parts(line[2:-2]))
            array_indices[name] = array_indices.get(name, 0) + 1
            table = ("__array_table__", name, array_indices[name])
            scopes.setdefault(table, {})
            continue
        if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
            name = tuple(_key_parts(line[1:-1]))
            table = resolve_table(name)
            if table in declared_tables:
                return (declared_tables[table], number, raw, table, 2)
            declared_tables[table] = number
            scopes.setdefault(table, {})
            continue
        eq = _find_eq(line)
        if eq < 0:
            continue
        parts = _key_parts(line[:eq].strip())
        key = tuple(parts)
        scope = scopes.setdefault(table, {})
        if key in scope:
            return (scope[key], number, raw, parts[0], 1)
        scope[key] = number
    return None


def _report_duplicate(source, filename, duplicate):
    first, second, raw, _key, column = duplicate
    lines = source.splitlines()
    width = len(str(second))
    print("error: conflicting keys", file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"  ┌─ {filename}:{second}:{column}", file=sys.stderr)
    print("  │", file=sys.stderr)
    for number in range(first, second + 1):
        print(f"{number:>{width}} │ {lines[number-1]}", file=sys.stderr)
        if number == first:
            print("  │ " + " " * (column - 1) + "- duplicate found here", file=sys.stderr)
        if number == second:
            print("  │ " + " " * (column - 1) + "^ duplicate key", file=sys.stderr)
    print("", file=sys.stderr)


def _syntax_error(source):
    """Return a rough (line, column, message) for common malformed TOML."""
    pending = ""
    start = 1
    for number, raw in enumerate(source.splitlines(), 1):
        line = _strip_comment(raw).strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue

def _format_diff(path, original, formatted):
    """Render Taplo's zero based, no context diff output."""
    if original == formatted:
        return ""
    import difflib
    old = original.splitlines()
    new = formatted.splitlines()
    matcher = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, old, new, autojunk=False)
    result = [f"diff a/{path} b/{path}\n", f"--- a/{path}\n", f"+++ b/{path}\n"]
    red, green, reset = "\x1b[31m", "\x1b[32m", "\x1b[0m"
    for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in matcher.get_opcodes():
        result.append(f"@@ -{i1},{i2-i1} +{j1},{j2-j1} @@\n")
        if tag in ("equal", "replace", "delete"):
            result.extend(line + "\n" for line in old[i1:i2] if tag == "equal")
            if tag != "equal":
                result.extend(f"{red}-{line}{reset}\n" for line in old[i1:i2])
        if tag in ("insert", "replace"):
            result.extend(f"{green}+{line}{reset}\n" for line in new[j1:j2])
    return "".join(result)

    lines = source.splitlines()

def _duplicates(source):
    scopes = {(): {}}
    table = ()
    array_indices = {}
    declared_tables = {}

    def resolve_table(parts):
        # A table nested below an array-of-tables belongs to the current array
        # element, so the same header may appear in each element.
        for size in range(len(parts) - 1, 0, -1):
            prefix = parts[:size]
            if prefix in array_indices:
                anchor = ("__array_table__", prefix, array_indices[prefix])
                return (anchor,) + parts[size:]
        return parts

    for number, raw in enumerate(source.splitlines(), 1):
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if line.startswith("[[") and line.endswith("]]" ):
            name = tuple(_key_parts(line[2:-2]))
            array_indices[name] = array_indices.get(name, 0) + 1
            table = ("__array_table__", name, array_indices[name])
            scopes.setdefault(table, {})
            continue
        if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
            name = tuple(_key_parts(line[1:-1]))
            table = resolve_table(name)
            # Subtables under an array-of-tables can be reopened within the
            # current element; they are not globally duplicated headers.
            nested_array_table = table != name
            if not nested_array_table:
                if table in declared_tables:
                    return (declared_tables[table], number, raw, table, 2)
                declared_tables[table] = number
                scopes.setdefault(table, {})
            else:
                # Taplo treats a reopened nested header as a fresh key scope.
                scopes[table] = {}
            continue
        eq = _find_eq(line)
        if eq < 0:
            continue
        following=lines[line_no] if line_no < len(lines) else ""
        print("error: invalid TOML", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"  ┌─ {filename}:{line_no}:{col}", file=sys.stderr)

        print(f"{line_no+1} │ │ {following}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("  │ ╰^ expected value", file=sys.stderr)
        print("", file=sys.stderr)
